newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia abolishes mineral export controls.
newsitem.headline: Australia abolishes mineral export controls.

text.p: The Australian Senate on Thursday abolished mineral export controls implemented in the 1970s as an attempt at price control.
Resources Minister Warwick Parer said in a statement that removal of the controls promised increased mineral exports.
The very threat of price controls over the years had forced customers to diversify to other suppliers, such as Canada and the United States, Parer said.
The Senate vote ended controls on bauxite, alumina, mineral sands, coal and liquefied natural gas.
Australian has retained export controls only over uranium, which must be regulated to meet international safeguards.
Parer said South Korea's Pohang Iron and Steel Co had told him last year that export controls had forced it to diversity.

"(But for the controls) we would be importing from Australia about 70 percent or 80 percent of the material supplied for our steel mills rather than 50 percent," Parer quoted the company's chief purchasing officer as saying.
For controlled resources Taiwan limited imports from Australia to 35 percent, Parer said.
"Underlying that is the uncertainty that exists because of the very existence of these export controls," he said.
